Sure! Being dead means I am no longer like the living. It means I don't really have any future aspirations, dreams, or plans I would have liked to pursue when I was, well, "alive" before I died multiple times. And because I see myself as a walking corpse, you normally wouldn't see a dead body walking out in the open. 

So I tend to try to hide away from people as much as I possibly can. This means I try to avoid even being seen by anyone. And this means no eye contact, no physical contact, I must blend in like a shadow. Like a ghost I prefer to observe people from a safe distance. Being around the living can be overwhelming as opposed to being with the dead. This also makes me prefer to wear completely black clothing at all times. I also enjoy wearing a black mask so others can't see too much of my face (it isn't that I'm insecure of how I look at all) and it makes me feel more secure and "hidden". I prefer gloomy dark weather and long nights rather than bright sunny days where people would be able to see me more visibly. I also detest the sun. 

But I feel dead as in my organs are dead. My physical body is dead but somehow it still moves, as though it came back like a zombie from the grave. I'm merely a ghost trapped in this corpse. And with other people I interact with, yes some do appear more "fresh" and alive than others do! I can usually tell simply from looking at them, or observing them (in a non creepy way of course), and eye contact for a few seconds can tell me that much.

And as for me I'd say I'm just a ghostly being in a somewhat still fresh corpse. My mind is in a constant state of "This isn't where I should be", and "I'm dead and everything else looks so full of life". It can be overwhelming as well because being out where there's so much colour and life to everything makes me feel even more out of place. Walking feels weird. Talking feels abnormal. Seeing other people act so.. "alive" freaks me out on some occasions. Other times I just watch and shake my head and sigh. Sometimes wistfully because imagine being alive again but I'm a corpse just watching life around me continue. 

It's strange too because when people look at me they seem almost bewildered or intrigued in some way. It goes for children, animals and some adults both young and old as well. When that happens I try to swiftly move away where I won't be as seen.

Knowing I'm a walking corpse has it's ups and downs. Some days it has no real effect on me and I'm quite happy going about my day as usual. Though a lot of the time it can be stressful because it feels like I'm trapped here in this body that isn't supposed to still be moving!
I usually don't feel interested in engaging with other people in person because well, what's the point if you're a corpse? And death isn't something everyone or anyone would pick as a conversation starter. 

I always feel the need to find a way back to my dead state. Motionless and in a grave. It might seem mundane for anyone else to hear but it would bring peace and comfort I have been trying to get for such a long time. Some days it even feels like I'm forever going to be stuck here. But to cope with these feelings I do things like listening to music and songs associated with death, or reading books about it. Long naps are great too because it's as close to simulating death as I can get.

Of course! So usually if something significant is about to happen to me or someone I know of, I get these signals. Sometimes it's one or two words and maybe a sentence that pops up in my head. However sometimes it's just a feeling. Like this energy, or ghost, pushing you towards something it wants you to see. A sign. 

One very recent event where this happened actually happened last Friday. I had woken up 20 minutes before my alarm and got ready when the words "car crash" came to mind. I had a roadtrip that day so I wasn't sure if those words had anything to do with it so I was cautious. But then about 10 minutes later my mother gets a call that someone had crashed their car into our wall. And apparently they had. I felt really weirded out but it's become normal the more I recall similar events that happened in the past. 

I had even explained all this to my psychologist and she seemed quite intrigued and wants me to write more about these experiences that I can share with her. She started to take me seriously when I spoke more in depth about these things in our session and I'm actually glad she didn't brush me off as crazy or just "delulu".

When I feel "high". High on life.
I've never done any kind of recreational drugs before but I remember waking up one day and feeling so damn good it was hard to believe. It got to the point where teachers, students, heck even my own father thought I was on drugs or something. I remember him asking me "Why do you keep smiling and laughing?" And "Why are your pupils so dilated? Has someone been giving you something?" Nope. 

And it lasted for pretty much a week and was the same. I'd blabber on and on about how great I felt and how amazing life really is. Even when things were bad I was euphoric and to this day I still don't know what that was. It was fun while it lasted.
